title: Bringing Machito to New York and planning a band
summary: He recalls sending for Machito, the dates in 1938 and 1941, and deciding to form his own band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: to organize a band for Machido, my brother-in-law. He's already here. I sent for him about six months before that.
I thought Machido came here in --

And I organized the band in '41. He was around with a little band -- he had a little band that played with the Sibonnet orchestra, and then he went to the G with the Buddy , was another club there, had a little six, seven piece band, nothing, amount to nothing, you know. So Latin music begin to develop.

There were Molina (phonetic) and Roggeda- (phonetic). I say, I'm going to get me a band. All right. So that's -- I started with Machido. I call the band to rehearsal. I already brought a few arrangements made especially. We got to the (inaudible). So, well, I say we macho (phonetic), you know, and (inaudible). I tell you don't leave this band (inaudible) don't worry about it. I've got the right kind of man here.
(Inaudible), you know (inaudible) we got the band,
start playing (inaudible) I left. I left the same way (inaudible). I don't know. Let's take a little rest now.
